howToPlay.title: How to play
howToPlay.goal: A group of players must work together to find the one Chameleon among them, while that player tries to avoid detection.
howToPlay.secret: Each round, players see the round's Secret — a style and a component, e.g. “Neumorphic · Toggle Switch”. The Chameleon is only told that a style and a component were drawn, and never learns which.
howToPlay.aim: Nobody is trying to finish it. You are making the code look like the Secret, not build one — enough that the others can see you know it, and not so much that the Chameleon works it out.
howToPlay.turns: Players take turns making one CSS edit each — name a property, give a value to one somebody else named, or add text. After everyone has had two turns, everyone votes on who they think the Chameleon is.
howToPlay.board: The screen shows the code as it grows, not the component it would render, and every edit is in its author's colour.
howToPlay.escape: The Chameleon wins if they don't get the majority vote.
howToPlay.steal: But even if the Chameleon gets caught, they get one chance to guess the Secret. Get both halves and they still win. Get one and they salvage a point.
howToPlay.points: First to five points takes the match.
howToPlay.table: Four to ten players, one screen everyone can see, and a device each.
